additions.node_text: רְשָׁעִים מְגֻלְגָּלִים בָּעֲשָׂבִים הַגְּדֵלִים עַל הַגַּגּוֹת
additions.reason: The Torah explicitly states that wicked people (רְשָׁעִים) are reincarnated (מְגֻלְגָּלִים) in the grasses growing on rooftops. This node is the subject of the entire teaching — the evil pole whose lack of elevation is the central problem. It is directly equated (זֶה בְּחִינַת) with Psalms 129:6. It belongs in Package 1 as the primary node of the evil cluster.
additions.source_quote: יֵשׁ רְשָׁעִים שֶׁהֵם מְגֻלְגָּלִים בָּעֲשָׂבִים הַגְּדֵלִים עַל הַגַּגּוֹת, וְאֵין לָהֶם עֲלִיָּה

additions.reason: The grasses on rooftops are the physical manifestation and bechina of the wicked souls — the two are explicitly equated in the text. The rooftop location is theologically significant: grasses on rooftops are unreachable by harvesters, do not fill anyone's hand (שֶׁלֹּא מִלֵּא כַפּוֹ קוֹצֵר per Psalms 129:7), and receive no blessing from passersby. This is the evil package's central metaphor.
additions.source_quote: יֵשׁ רְשָׁעִים שֶׁהֵם מְגֻלְגָּלִים בָּעֲשָׂבִים הַגְּדֵלִים עַל הַגַּגּוֹת, וְאֵין לָהֶם עֲלִיָּה, כִּי אֵין קוֹצְרִין אוֹתָן הָעֲשָׂבִים

additions.reason: The Psalms verse (129:6) 'יִהְיוּ כְּחָצִיר גַּגּוֹת' is explicitly cited as the bechina of the wicked reincarnated in rooftop grasses. The full verse implies drying without elevation: 'which withers before it grows up, of which the reaper does not fill his hand.' This is the scriptural anchor of the evil package, sharing essential nature with the wicked (Package 1).
additions.source_quote: זֶה בְּחִינַת (תהילים קכ״ט:ו׳): יִהְיוּ כְּחָצִיר גַּגּוֹת וְכוּ', שֶׁלֹּא מִלֵּא כַפּוֹ קוֹצֵר וְכוּ'

additions.reason: The harvested grain is the positive counterpart to the rooftop grasses. It is reaped — meaning selected and lifted — and therefore receives the blessing of God from passersby, and thereby achieves elevation. It is the dominant node of Package 2 because it connects to both the mechanism (harvesting) and the outcome (blessing + elevation). The contrast with the rooftop grasses makes clear that being harvested IS the defining bechina of the elevated soul.
additions.source_quote: אֲבָל אוֹתָהּ הַתְּבוּאָה שֶׁקּוֹצְרִין, אוֹמְרִים הָעוֹבְרִים בִּרְכַּת ה' כַּנַּ"ל, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לָהּ עֲלִיָּה

additions.reason: Saying 'Birkat Hashem' (the greeting/blessing 'Hashem should help you' — ה' יַעְזֹר — said by passersby to harvesters) is explicitly linked to the elevation of the grain. Its absence from the rooftop grasses explains their lack of elevation. In the good domain, בִּרְכַּת ה' is the bechina of divine acknowledgment and connection — it is the essential quality of the harvested grain that makes its elevation possible. It shares the same essential nature as the elevated grain: both are expressions of divine favor extended to that which has been chosen.
additions.source_quote: אוֹמְרִים הָעוֹבְרִים בִּרְכַּת ה' כַּנַּ"ל, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לָהּ עֲלִיָּה; וְלֹא אָמְרוּ הָעוֹבְרִים בִּרְכַּת ה' וְכוּ', וְעַל כֵּן אֵין לָהֶם עֲלִיָּה

additions.reason: Elevation/ascent (עֲלִיָּה) is the outcome-concept that defines the good pole. It is what the wicked souls lack (אֵין לָהֶם עֲלִיָּה) and what the harvested grain achieves (יֵשׁ לָהּ עֲלִיָּה). In bechina terms, עֲלִיָּה is not merely a result of blessing — it IS the same thing as being blessed-and-harvested. The elevated soul and the blessed grain share one essential nature. This node connects to both תְּבוּאָה הַנִּקְצֶרֶת and בִּרְכַּת ה', making it the conceptual hub of Package 2.

good_evil_mirror.description: Torah #227 has a clear good/evil mirror structure: the wicked-as-rooftop-grasses (Package 1, evil) is the exact mirror of the harvested grain that rises (Package 2, good). The mirroring is expressed through three paired opposites: (1) אֵין קוֹצְרִין vs. קוֹצְרִין; (2) לֹא אָמְרוּ הָעוֹבְרִים בִּרְכַּת ה' vs. אוֹמְרִים הָעוֹבְרִים בִּרְכַּת ה'; (3) אֵין לָהֶם עֲלִיָּה vs. יֵשׁ לָהּ עֲלִיָּה.

analysis_notes.structural_observation: Torah #227 is an extremely brief teaching (3 sentences). Its structure is entirely binary — two poles with no neutral structural nodes, no letters, no body parts. The teaching's central mechanism (the role of the passersby who say Birkat Hashem to harvesters) suggests that the Tzaddik or community plays the role of the mevarchim (those who pronounce the blessing), but this is not explicitly stated with bechina language.
